name: House of Nobles
summary: The House of Nobles is the hereditary aristocratic council that helps administer the kingdom of Stormwind from Stormwind Keep. Holding immense leverage over regional land, taxation, and trade, their refusal to pay the rebuilt city's laborers ignited the bloody riots that gave birth to the Defias Brotherhood.

sections.title: Aristocrats of the Realm
sections.body: Composed of Stormwind's most powerful patrician bloodlines, the House of Nobles serves as the primary advisory body to the Crown. Because the aristocracy owns the majority of the arable land throughout Elwynn, Westfall, and Duskwood, they wield outsized authority over commerce, regional magistrates, and royal decrees. While the boy-king Anduin Wrynn and Highlord Bolvar Fordragon officially rule the kingdom, the council routinely ties the throne's hands in red tape, asserting the power to stall trials, block executions, and meddle in provincial administration.

sections.title: The Labor Revolt
sections.body: Following the Second War, the House of Nobles contracted Guildmaster Edwin VanCleef and the Stonemasons Guild to rebuild Stormwind City from its ashes. However, the nobility simultaneously incurred staggering debts while expanding the kingdom's military frontier south into Stranglethorn. When the gleaming capital was finished, the nobles balked at the invoice and refused to pay the workers their full wages. Enraged by the betrayal, the masons rioted in the streets. A stone thrown during the chaos struck and killed Queen Tiffin Wrynn, prompting the nobility to banish the guild, driving the ruined workers into Westfall to form the Defias Brotherhood.

sections.title: Bureaucratic Paralysis
sections.body: With King Varian missing, the nobles have largely abandoned the kingdom's outlying territories to fend for themselves while exploiting royal authority for petty squabbles. Officials in Darkshire seethe because the House of Nobles countermanded their death sentence for the grave robber Dextren Ward, ordering him spared and transferred to the Stormwind Stockade instead. Similarly, the execution of the Blackrock Orc chieftain Targorr the Dread has been indefinitely delayed simply because a scheming noble wishes to use the monster as a political pawn, leaving local sentries to watch Stormwind rot from within.

sections.title: Whispers of Treason
sections.body: The council's obstinacy is far from simple greed. In truth, Lady Katrana Prestor—secretly the black dragon Onyxia—has systematically manipulated the House of Nobles to paralyze the kingdom. By stoking the aristocracy's arrogance during the stonemason negotiations and encouraging them to hoard royal funds, she orchestrated both the realm's internal collapse and the King's kidnapping. High-ranking aristocrats like Lord Gregor Lescovar actively conspire alongside the Defias Brotherhood in the shadow of the throne, ensuring no imperial troops march to save the outlying towns.

faq.q: What is the House of Nobles?
aliases: what is the house of nobles
who are the nobles in stormwind
faq.answer: The House of Nobles is Stormwind's ruling aristocratic assembly, composed of prominent landowning families whose titles and seats are passed down through inheritance. They serve as advisors to the monarch and control much of the kingdom's domestic policy, taxes, and labor laws.

faq.q: Why did the House of Nobles refuse to pay the Stonemasons?
faq.answer: The nobility heavily overextended Stormwind's treasury by financing costly military expeditions southward into Elwynn and Stranglethorn. When Edwin VanCleef presented the bill for rebuilding Stormwind City, the nobles could not pay, offering a fraction of what was promised and eventually ordering the guild disbanded.

aliases: who threw the rock at the queen
faq.answer: During the stonemason riots sparked by the House of Nobles' refusal to pay, an unidentified rioter threw a paving stone into the crowd. It struck Queen Tiffin Wrynn in the head, killing her instantly and permanently derailing any peaceful negotiations between the crown and the workers.

faq.q: Why won't Stormwind send troops to help Westfall or Duskwood?
faq.answer: The House of Nobles controls the realm's purse strings and administrative authorizations. The nobility continuously blocks funding, military deployments, and municipal aid to outlying territories, leaving local militias like the People's Militia and the Night Watch entirely isolated.

faq.q: Who was Lord Baurles K. Wishock?
faq.answer: Lord Baurles K. Wishock is an influential noble lobbying for an investigation of the warlocks beneath The Slaughtered Lamb. The consequences of his inquiry are uncovered in the warlock quest chain.

faq.q: Did all the nobles turn against the Stonemasons?
faq.answer: No. Queen Tiffin Wrynn originally supported the masons, as did Count S. J. Erlgadin, who lobbied fiercely to improve their wages and working conditions. Erlgadin grew so disgusted by his peers' betrayal of the guild that he renounced his title and seat entirely, fleeing society to join Hemet Nesingwary's expedition in Stranglethorn.

angles.text: For humans of Westfall and Duskwood, the House of Nobles represents arrogant highborn who sit comfortably in their marble palace while common folk bleed to defend their homesteads from bandits and monsters.
The nobility's bitter squabbles, corrupt dealings, and dirty secrets provide ample work for fixers, cutpurses, and the master cheesemonger Elling Trias.
Stormwind's practitioners of the dark arts beneath The Slaughtered Lamb face unwanted inquiries from influential nobles.

While powerful within Stormwind City's court, the House of Nobles holds little sway over the wider Grand Alliance, though their stinginess constantly threatens the southern human territories' stability.
